decision.reasoning: Evaluating role scope/seniority rather than compa-ratio gap size: - NYX-001 (L7, compa-ratio 0.37): Despite the severe compa-ratio gap and large retention award, the role summary describes a new-grad IC working under supervision on a single sub-block (CDC synchronizer and register-map RTL) of one component, with one tapeout and no direct reports. This is a junior, narrowly-scoped role regardless of the L7 level label — the described scope (single sub-block, supervised, no leadership) does not indicate broad organizational criticality or irreplaceable expertise. Losing this person is a routine backfill, not a strategic loss. Not flagged as critical. - NYX-007 (L3, compa-ratio 0.76): Described as a "strong contributor" involved in cache coherence modeling *discussions* for the current core project. This indicates participation, not ownership or unique authority over a critical workstream. L3 is a relatively junior level, and the scope described (participating in discussions) doesn't show singular indispensability. Not flagged as critical. - NYX-013 (L3, compa-ratio 0.77): Described as a strong analog designer "picking up more responsibility" including "some layout review" on the PMIC team. This suggests growing scope but still developing responsibility rather than owning a critical function or possessing scarce, hard-to-replace expertise. L3 level and the tentative language ("picking up," "some") indicate this is not yet a role whose loss would be a major organizational blow. None of the three underwater employees have role descriptions indicating broad scope, unique/scarce expertise, leadership responsibility, or ownership of a critical, hard-to-replace function. All three are individual contributors at junior-to-mid levels with narrow or still-developing scope. Based on role scope and seniority evidence alone (independent of compa-ratio magnitude), none rise to the level of genuinely critical-to-retain in this list. If more senior/broader-scope underwater employees existed (e.g., a sole technical authority, a manager with critical direct reports, or an owner of a program-critical workstream), those would be flagged; these three do not meet that bar based on the evidence given.
